motivation: The supported pre-loss run-length effect may reflect current source-year meadow abundance/detectability rather than historical local legacy. Test whether run length remains informative after source-year focal frequency and Braun-Blanquet state are added.

primary_population.sequence_rule: same frozen 259 exact-point three-year Thalassia-loss sequences
primary_population.source_year_join: join annual node-level focal_frequency and bb_cover_mean_all_points on node_id x source_year
primary_population.missing_rule: retain only sequences with both source-year quantitative state values observed; do not impute

model.outcome: Thalassia recorded present at the same meter mark in the recovery year
model.preprocessing: node-center run length first; StandardScaler numeric predictors; OneHot stable node identity

primary_hypothesis.statement: Longer-than-usual exact-point pre-loss Thalassia history remains positively associated with one-year re-recording after controlling current source-year focal frequency and Braun-Blanquet state.
primary_hypothesis.estimator: coefficient of standardized within-node centered pre_loss_run_length

secondary_descriptive: same model without current source-year frequency/BB for coefficient orientation only
correlations of run length with source-year frequency and Braun-Blanquet
return/nonreturn medians of source-year frequency and Braun-Blanquet

interpretation.supported: Pre-loss local occupancy history contains recovery information beyond current transect-level abundance and stable node identity, strengthening a genuine history/legacy interpretation while remaining mechanistically unresolved.
interpretation.unsupported: The pre-loss run-length effect is absorbed by current source-year quantitative state; current meadow abundance/detectability is sufficient to explain the apparent history signal.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc saturation audit of an already-opened recovery endpoint.
A surviving history effect would still not prove clonal memory or residual rhizomes; fine-scale habitat quality and repeated detectability remain alternatives.
Current focal frequency and Braun-Blanquet are transect-level states, not point-level physiological measures.
Return means recorded reappearance, not genet-level recolonization.
Do not change the annual-state controls, history definition, node-centering, model, bootstrap unit, minima, or support threshold after opening the endpoint.
